title: Visual encoding: position, length, angle, area, colour and shape

videos.script: Here is a table with five numbers in it. Horta's orders last year, one number for each region of Brazil. {{table}} Read it, and tell me which region is second largest. You can. It takes a few seconds. {{read}} Now look at the same five numbers as bars. {{bars}} The answer arrives before you have decided to look for it. That speed is the whole reason charts exist. {{fast}} A chart turns each number into something the eye measures without effort. A position. A length. An angle. An area. A shade of colour. {{channels}} Those are called channels, and they are not equal. Some the eye reads precisely. Some it reads badly. And one of them, hue, cannot say which number is bigger at all. {{unequal}} This lesson names the channels and shows the same five numbers in six of them. Then it sets up the computer you will draw on for the rest of the course. {{plan}} By the end you will have drawn your first chart, and you will know what it is made of. {{end}}
